title: GPU-Based Parallel BP Decoding for Quantum LDPC Memory
abstract: Quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) decoding requires reliable corrections and low latency over long syndrome histories. We extend BP-SF, an oscillation-guided belief-propagation (BP) decoder with independent syndrome-flip trials, by introducing windowed and streaming operations. Our CUDA implementation combines disordered-memory retries, sliding windows, correlation-aware graphs, and layered scheduling. Circuit-level simulations test fixed-basis memory and complete logical Pauli-frame recovery. On the [[144,12,12]] bivariate bicycle code at physical error rate p = 0.002, parallel BP-SF reduces 99.9th-percentile call latency by a factor of 13.15 relative to an eight-chain Relay-BP GPU baseline on 100,000 matched samples for which every tested method's initial BP stage fails within 80 iterations. Windowed BP-SF maintains a flat logical error rate and nearly constant per-round compute time through 512 rounds, reaching a 17.1-fold speedup over monolithic decoding. In 512-round full-frame streaming decoding with 2.97-ms syndrome arrivals, layered BP-SF on a transformed joint graph with 20 retries reduces 99.9th-percentile correction-release age from 166.29 to 36.25 ms relative to the joint graph with flooding updates and 100 retries. These results connect parallel BP post-processing to lower decoding costs and earlier correction release in streaming quantum memory.

bite.hook: A new GPU-based decoder for quantum memory achieves a 17.1-fold speedup in syndrome processing.
tldr: The researchers created 'Windowed BP-SF', an optimized GPU decoder for quantum LDPC codes using sliding windows and parallel processing.
They implemented the decoder using CUDA, incorporating disordered-memory retries and layered scheduling to handle syndrome histories.
Testing on a [[144,12,12]] code showed significant reductions in latency and correction-release age compared to standard baseline methods.
bite.whyItMatters: Decoding quantum errors in real-time is a major bottleneck for quantum computing; faster, parallelized software is critical for keeping quantum memory stable.
bite.eli5: Imagine a library where books are constantly being misplaced. A 'decoder' is the librarian who finds the errors. This new method uses a super-fast computer to check many shelves at once, fixing the library's organization much faster than the old, one-shelf-at-a-time method.

glossary.shortDef: Belief Propagation with Syndrome-Flip; an algorithm for correcting errors in quantum codes.
glossary.eli5Def: A smart guessing game where the computer repeatedly updates its best guess about where errors occurred until it finds the right fix.

glossary.shortDef: Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check codes; codes that protect quantum information from noise.
glossary.eli5Def: A special code designed to protect fragile quantum information from getting corrupted by the environment.
